background_notes.fact: For a finite family of Lebesgue-integrable real functions g_k and real constants a_k, Σ_k a_k g_k is integrable and its integral is Σ_k a_k∫g_k. background_notes.justification: Finite linear combinations remain absolutely integrable by the triangle inequality. Linearity of the Lebesgue integral follows by decomposing integrable functions into positive and negative parts, where all resulting integral values are finite; iterating gives finite-sum linearity. Euclidean bilinearity identifies the combined function with the displayed finite combination. Equality of functions gives equality of their integrals, and zero integrates to zero. Empty spatial sums when n=0 obey the same identities.

background_notes.fact: If E is differentiable at every r>0 with derivative zero and f:ℝ→ℝ equals E on (0,∞), then f has derivative zero and is continuous at every r>0. Consequently for 0<s<t it is continuous on [s,t] and has derivative zero at every point of (s,t).

background_notes.justification: For r>0, the neighborhood (r−r/2,r+r/2) is contained in positive times. Thus f and E have identical difference quotients near r and the same derivative. Differentiability implies continuity: the difference f(r+h)−f(r) is h times a quotient tending to the finite derivative, and hence tends to zero. Pointwise continuity on a neighborhood of each point of [s,t] implies continuity restricted to that interval. This supplies precisely M004's continuity and derivative hypotheses without any behavior at zero.
